questions.question: What prefix should each ticket title get?

options.label: Repo nickname [FF]/[AH]/[DSA]
options.description: Prefix titles with the repo's short nickname, matching your session-title [NICK] convention. e.g. '[FF] security: bulk user password reset'. Makes issues scannable by repo in any GitHub view. Some ai-harness titles already use [AH].

options.label: Primary domain label [security] etc.
options.description: Prefix with the issue's main GitHub label, e.g. '[security] ...', '[ci] ...', '[ops] ...'. FamilyFund has a domain taxonomy; ai-harness/dstrader-aws have no labels so they'd get none.

options.label: Board name [Trading & Fund]
options.description: Prefix with the GitHub Project board the ticket lives on. Coarser than repo nickname.

options.label: FamilyFund only
options.description: Only retitle FamilyFund issues. Leaves ai-harness, dstrader-aws, and Job Search drafts untouched.

options.label: All boards, all open issues
options.description: Retitle every open issue across FamilyFund, ai-harness, and dstrader-aws (Todo + In Progress + any open). Draft notes can't be edited via gh and would be skipped.

options.label: All boards, Todo only
options.description: Only the available (Status=Todo) issues shown in the list, across all three boards.

transcript_tail.text: Now clean up the ad-hoc worktree.

Done. The `todo` list now shows GitHub labels.

**What changed** (ai-harness `cmd_todo` in `skills/start-work/scripts/agent_claims.sh`, merged to `main` as `b15362c` and pushed):

- `gh project item-list` doesn't carry issue labels, so `cmd_todo` now fetches them once per distinct repo via `gh issue list --json number,labels` and appends them in `[brackets]` after each ticket.
- The cache is a newline-delimited `repo#num<TAB>labels` string with pure parameter-expansion lookup — your only bash is macOS 3.2, which has no associative arrays (my first `declare -A` attempt failed; this is why). The trailing-TAB anchor keeps `#1` from matching `#16`.
- One extra API call per repo (~3 total), not per ticket.
- Updated the SKILL.md `todo` description to mention the labels.

The skill file is a symlink into the canonical ai-harness checkout, so the change is live now (verified). FamilyFund tickets show their taxonomy — e.g. `#16 [security,epic]`, `#30 [ops]`, `#63 [enhancement,blocked]`. ai-harness/dstrader-aws issues show none because those repos haven't applied the label set.

I made the edit in a throwaway ai-harness worktree, merged `--ff-only` to `main`, pushed, and removed the worktree + branch.
